question.problem: Consider the equation $2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-3=0$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the numerical value of ${x}_{2}+{x}_{4}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-3 & =0 \\ 2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & =3 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2x & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2x & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 2x & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{60}^{∘}}{2}+\frac{n\cdot {360}^{∘}}{2} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{{120}^{∘}}{2}+\frac{n\cdot {360}^{∘}}{2} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={30}^{∘}$ and $x={60}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={210}^{∘}$ and $x={240}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x={30}^{∘},{60}^{∘},{210}^{∘},{240}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}={60}^{∘}$ and ${x}_{4}={240}^{∘},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}+{x}_{4}=60+240=300.
$$
